name: Flow matching
definition: Learn a time-dependent velocity field by matching target velocities along a chosen path. At inference, integrate the learned field to transport an initial state.
caveat: The starting state and meaning of time differ across these papers. A shared learning family does not imply the same task.

uses.role: Separate morphology and intensity evolution for disease forecasting.
Learn residual transport from a coarse APN image to an HR target.
Keep a pretrained field fixed; change how its ODE is solved.

name: Rectified flow
definition: The DRIFT training path interpolates linearly between a coarse estimate and the target, with target velocity equal to their difference.
caveat: A straight training interpolation does not make a learned numerical inference trajectory exact in one step.

uses.role: Residual image refinement after anatomical projection.
Related flow-model background; the contribution is a solver, not rectified-flow training.

name: ODE sampling
definition: Numerically integrate a neural velocity field over a time interval to obtain a terminal state. Each solver evaluation calls the field model.
caveat: A solver step, a sequential iteration, and a total network evaluation need not be the same quantity.

uses.role: Thickness chooses the number of Euler refinements.
Tentative states at multiple schedule times are evaluated concurrently.
Integrate morphology and intensity fields in a forecasting pipeline.

name: NFE
definition: Number of function evaluations: how many times a neural vector field is evaluated.
caveat: ParaFlow reports total NFEs across parallel evaluations. DRIFT’s velocity NFEs exclude APN and preprocessing.

uses.role: Total workload can increase while sequential iterations decrease.
AIS allocates 0–15 velocity-network evaluations in the main setting.

name: Parallel fixed-point iteration
definition: Update multiple trajectory guesses using vector-field evaluations from the previous iteration, then repeat until a convergence criterion is met.
caveat: Parallel evaluations require hardware and memory; the theoretical bound alone does not guarantee a wall-clock speedup.

uses.role: Triangular trajectory equations solved in a sliding window.

name: Diffusion / generative modeling
definition: These papers use or study existing image generators that iteratively transform a latent or token state into an image. Their exact generation objectives vary.
caveat: Do not equate every image-generation architecture with the same diffusion or flow formulation.

uses.role: Studies discrete/continuous diffusion and autoregressive UMM families.
LightningDiT learns the concatenated frequency-aware latent distribution.
Evaluates flow-matching models SD3 and FLUX.

name: Haar DWT
definition: A fixed discrete wavelet transform separates coarse information from directional detail bands. In 2D there is one LL and three detail bands; in 3D one LLL and seven detail bands per level.
caveat: The same transform plays different roles: learned representation in DeBaT versus training augmentation in KernelWave.

uses.role: Split 2D image bands before training separate encoders and decoders.
Scale 3D detail coefficients to make smooth/sharp training images.

name: Frequency / high-frequency detail
definition: High spatial frequencies describe rapid spatial variations such as fine textures and boundaries. Low frequencies describe more slowly varying structure.
caveat: High frequency is not synonymous with useful anatomy: it can also include noise. Frequency processing here includes Haar, FFT, DoG, and bandwidth reasoning.

uses.role: Protect fine details inside the tokenizer.
Approximate CT reconstruction-related frequency shifts.
Use FFT features and k-space simulation to derive a prior.
Model thickness-related loss of through-plane bandwidth.
Use Difference-of-Gaussians lesion-texture guidance at inference.

name: Latent representation
definition: An encoded representation used between image input/output and the model’s central computation. Its structure controls what information can be carried forward.
caveat: A shared representation is not automatically a better compressed representation; the papers measure different outcomes.

uses.role: Concatenate separate low/high learned codes at a matched total size.
Probe how unified versus separate visual representations affect transfer.
Samples the existing model state without redesigning its representation.

name: MRI
definition: Magnetic resonance images are the medical inputs or outputs of several papers in this collection. The tasks concern different stages of the imaging workflow.
caveat: Shared modality does not imply shared output: masks, super-resolved scans, and future scans answer different questions.

uses.role: Segment tumors in reconstructed brain MRI.
Reconstruct finer through-plane resolution.
Forecast future brain images and lesion progression.

name: k-space sampling
definition: MRI measurements encode spatial frequencies. A sampling operator selects which measurements contribute to a reconstructed image.
caveat: This is acquisition sampling, not generative sampling. SPHERE estimates sampling-related parameters from already reconstructed images.

uses.role: Predict parameters, simulate perturbations, then derive a structural prior.

name: Deformation vector field
definition: A spatial field that assigns a displacement vector to each location, allowing one image or feature grid to be warped toward another.
caveat: SPHERE’s field is an acquisition-related structural proxy; PDF’s warp comes from predicted lesion evolution.

uses.role: Guide feature alignment and retention with a sampling-induced proxy.
Estimate dense optical-flow displacement between lesion masks.

name: Slice thickness / PAD
definition: Slice thickness controls through-plane signal integration. DRIFT uses 1 − target thickness / input thickness as a normalized bandwidth-deficit cue.
caveat: PAD is metadata-based severity, not a learned per-image difficulty score.

uses.role: Condition both stages and set the AIS refinement budget.

name: Physics-informed learning
definition: Use structure motivated by an acquisition mechanism or disease-dynamics model to guide a learned method.
caveat: A physics-inspired proxy or soft regularizer does not establish exact physical or biological fidelity.

uses.role: Sampling-related DVF guides segmentation.
Diffusion–reaction–advection span constrains morphology velocity.
SLR slice-profile simulation and thickness-based bandwidth cue.

name: Fisher-KPP
definition: A reaction–diffusion formulation combines spatial spread with a logistic local-growth term. PDF adds advection to account for transport.
caveat: PDF constructs a normalized concentration proxy from lesion masks; it does not measure biological cell density.

uses.role: Provides the components for a physics-inspired span.

name: PDE regularization
definition: In PDF, project the morphology velocity onto a span of spatial diffusion, reaction and advection components; penalize the squared residual.
caveat: The loss is soft. It does not embed an exact PDE solver in the inference process.

uses.role: Regularizes morphology training alongside the flow-matching objective.

name: Medical segmentation
definition: Predict a region mask identifying the anatomy or pathology of interest.
caveat: The scope differs: brain MRI, universal 2D medical tasks, and candidate-centered 3D tumors are not interchangeable benchmarks.

uses.role: Brain tumor masks informed by an MRI acquisition prior.
Prompt-free foreground/background masks across modalities.
3D tumor masks from localized candidate patches.

name: Cross-domain generalization
definition: Evaluate whether a trained model works on a different dataset, acquisition condition, or modality without simply retraining on that test domain.
caveat: Different papers use different protocols. Do not rank robustness from scores on unrelated datasets.

uses.role: BraTS 2023 training, BraTS 2019/MSD testing.
Unseen datasets and unseen modalities, with explicit EM failure.
Leave-one-domain-out evaluation across CT sources.
Zero-shot real thick-slice MRI and unseen input thickness.

name: Multimodal learning
definition: Learn from different kinds of input or information. Here the term can refer to text/images or to heterogeneous medical imaging modalities.
caveat: C2P uses medical modalities and offline image–text distillation; Transferability studies understanding/generation in unified vision–language systems.

uses.role: Unify image understanding and generation through shared or coupled models.
Separate modality-conditioned semantics from shared geometry.

name: Cross-task transfer
definition: Train a capability in one task and test whether the same capability improves in another task without directly training that second task in the intervention.
caveat: Transfer varies with architecture, task, and direction; comparative evidence is not a universal causal law.

uses.role: Counting, layout and text probes test understanding ↔ generation.

name: Geometry tokens
definition: Learned tokens explicitly supervised with attributes derived from masks, such as area, bounding box and centroid.
caveat: The token prior can fail when the test structure has a topology unlike the training structures.

uses.role: Guide dynamic segmentation and check inference-view self-consistency.

name: Dynamic convolution
definition: Generate convolution parameters conditioned on the current input instead of using one fixed output classifier for all inputs.
caveat: This describes input-specific weights, not training new weights at test time.

uses.role: TGDH generates foreground/background weights from tokens and image context.

name: Mixed / weak supervision
definition: Combine dense voxel masks with less detailed labels, here bounding boxes. A box localizes an object without tracing its exact boundary.
caveat: Mixed supervision differs from unlabeled-data semi-supervision. More weak labels can hurt when domains or task weights are poorly balanced.

uses.role: Jointly exploit mask-labelled CT and box-only PN9.

name: Dice / DSC
definition: An overlap measure: twice the intersection divided by the total size of the two masks. Higher means stronger overlap.
caveat: Some papers report a fraction, others a percentage. Overlap alone can hide boundary mistakes.

uses.role: Tumor-region Dice percentages.
Dataset and average segmentation Dice percentages.
3D lesion DSC percentages.
Future-lesion DSC fractions.

name: HD95
definition: The 95th-percentile boundary-distance metric used to assess segmentation boundary errors. Lower is better.
caveat: Do not confuse it with maximum Hausdorff distance (HD), which PDF reports. SPHERE’s printed Eq. 25 shows maxima despite its HD95 prose; follow the named table metric cautiously.

uses.role: Reported Hausdorff95 tumor-boundary evaluation.
Boundary metric alongside DSC.

name: PSNR
definition: Peak signal-to-noise ratio expresses image reconstruction error relative to the intensity dynamic range, in decibels. Higher is better for this distortion measure.
caveat: High whole-image PSNR can coexist with poor prediction of a small changing lesion.

uses.role: Volumetric super-resolution fidelity.
Whole-image future-scan similarity; compare with lesion metrics.

name: SSIM
definition: Structural similarity compares image luminance, contrast and structural information. Higher is better for this metric.
caveat: An image-quality score is not a validation of biological or clinical correctness.

uses.role: Average across slices in axial, coronal and sagittal directions.
Image-level similarity for longitudinal forecasting.

name: FID / rFID / gFID
definition: Compare image distributions using statistics of pretrained Inception features. Lower indicates closer feature distributions to the chosen reference.
caveat: The reference matters: Transferability compares against baseline-generated images; DeBaT distinguishes reconstruction and generation FID.

uses.role: FID to the baseline generator measures distribution shift.
rFID for reconstructed images and gFID for generated images.
Generation-quality comparison at different solver settings.
